target_customer: Working professionals and students in one Indian city who want home-style meals without cooking daily.
competitors: Cloud kitchens and food-delivery apps such as Swiggy and Zomato (unverified, from general knowledge)
Local tiffin services and mess providers (unverified)
Other home chefs on social media (unverified)
failure_reasons: Home-kitchen capacity limits orders, so growth stalls quickly.
Licensing or hygiene problems can stop sales overnight.
Delivery cost and delays erode the margin on a low-priced meal.

compliance_flags.note: Selling food, even from a home kitchen, usually needs food-safety registration or licence; check requirements for your city. Verify with official sources; this is not legal advice.
Packaged food and bakery items carry labelling and hygiene rules. Verify with official sources; this is not legal advice.
Registration may depend on turnover thresholds. Verify with official sources; this is not legal advice.

market_saturation.justification: Delivery apps, cloud kitchens and local tiffin services are plentiful.

operational_complexity.justification: Daily cooking, packing and delivery must be reliable from one kitchen.

compliance.justification: Food licensing and hygiene rules apply even to home-based sellers.

capital_need.justification: Equipment and packaging are cheap to start.

founder_load.justification: The founder cooks, delivers, markets and handles customers alone.

suggested_pivots: Begin with a small pre-order group to prove repeat demand before buying equipment.
Focus on one product, such as baked snacks, that travels well and has a better margin.
